The '''93rd Academy Awards''' ceremony, presented by the [[Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences]] (AMPAS), honored films released from January 1, 2020, to February 28, 2021, at [[Union Station (Los Angeles)|Union Station]] in [[Los Angeles]].{{efn|name=Oscar}} The ceremony was held on April 25, 2021, rather than its usual late-February date due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Academy Delays 2021 Oscars Ceremony Because of Coronavirus |url=https://www.tampabay.com/news/nation-world/2020/06/15/academy-delays-2021-oscars-ceremony-because-of-coronavirus/ |access-date=August 12, 2020 |work=[[Tampa Bay Times]] |date=June 15, 2020 |archive-date=June 17, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200617160434/https://www.tampabay.com/news/nation-world/2020/06/15/academy-delays-2021-oscars-ceremony-because-of-coronavirus/ |url-status=live}}</ref> During the ceremony, the AMPAS presented [[Academy Awards]] (commonly referred to as Oscars) in 23 categories. The ceremony, televised in the United States by [[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]], was produced by Jesse Collins, [[Stacey Sher]], and [[Steven Soderbergh]], and was directed by [[Glenn Weiss]].<ref name="Producers"/><ref>{{cite news |last1=Hipes |first1=Patrick |title=Oscars Production Team a Mix Of Veterans And Newcomers Including Questlove, Richard LaGravenese, Dream Hampton |url=https://deadline.com/2021/03/oscars-production-team-2021-questlove-richard-lagravenese-dream-walker-1234721037/ |access-date=March 25, 2021 |work=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |date=March 24, 2021 |archive-date=March 24, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210324190347/https://deadline.com/2021/03/oscars-production-team-2021-questlove-richard-lagravenese-dream-walker-1234721037/ |url-status=live}}</ref> For the third consecutive year, the ceremony had no official host.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Freiman |first1=Jordan |title=Oscars 2021: Full list of winners and nominees |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/oscars-2021-winners-list-nominees/ |access-date=June 19, 2021 |agency=[[CBS News]] |date=April 26, 2021 |archive-date=June 1, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210601192221/https://www.cbsnews.com/news/oscars-2021-winners-list-nominees/ |url-status=live}}</ref> In related events, the [[Academy Scientific and Technical Award]]s were presented by host [[Nia DaCosta]] on February 13, 2021, in a virtual ceremony.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Welk |first1=Brian |title=Oscars Present 17 Awards for Technical and Scientific Achievement |url=https://www.thewrap.com/oscars-present-17-awards-for-technical-and-scientific-achievement/ |access-date=May 12, 2021 |work=[[TheWrap]] |date=February 2, 2021 |archive-date=June 24, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210624203132/https://www.thewrap.com/oscars-present-17-awards-for-technical-and-scientific-achievement/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

''[[Nomadland]]'' won three awards at the main ceremony, including [[Academy Award for Best Picture|Best Picture]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Lowry |first1=Brian |title=Academy Awards 2021: 'Nomadland' wins Best Picture At an Oscars That Spreads the Wealth |url=https://www.cnn.com/2021/04/25/entertainment/academy-awards-2021/index.html |access-date=April 27, 2021 |agency=[[CNN]] |date=April 26, 2021 |archive-date=April 27, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210427024819/https://www.cnn.com/2021/04/25/entertainment/academy-awards-2021/index.html |url-status=live}}</ref> Other winners included ''[[The Father (2020 film)|The Father]]'', ''[[Judas and the Black Messiah]]'', ''[[Ma Rainey's Black Bottom (film)|Ma Rainey's Black Bottom]]'', ''[[Mank]]'', ''[[Soul (2020 film)|Soul]]'' and ''[[Sound of Metal]]'' with two awards each, and ''[[Another Round]]'', ''[[Colette (2020 film)|Colette]]'', ''[[If Anything Happens I Love You]]'', ''[[Minari]]'', ''[[My Octopus Teacher]]'', ''[[Promising Young Woman]]'', ''[[Tenet]]'', and ''[[Two Distant Strangers]]'' with one. The telecast received mostly negative reviews, and it garnered 10.4 million viewers, making it the least-watched Oscar broadcast since viewership records began [[46th Academy Awards|for the 46th ceremony in 1974]].<ref name=DeadlineViews/><ref name="Makeover">{{cite news |last1=Lang |first1=Brett |last2=Setodeh |first2=Ramin |last3=Riley |first3=Jenelle |last4=Gleiberman |first4=Owen |last5=Debruge |first5=Peter |title=After Oscars Ratings Tank, Do the Academy Awards Need Another Makeover? |url=https://variety.com/2021/awards/news/oscars-2021-academy-awards-reviews-ratings-1234962181/ |access-date=June 19, 2021 |work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=April 28, 2021 |archive-date=May 3, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210503143925/https://variety.com/2021/awards/news/oscars-2021-academy-awards-reviews-ratings-1234962181/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="BBC Review">{{cite news |title=Oscars 2021: Audiences Turn Away As a Sluggish Ceremony Leaves Critics Cold |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/entertainment-arts-56885646 |access-date=July 13, 2021 |agency=[[BBC News]] |date=April 26, 2021 |archive-date=August 4, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210804113257/https://www.bbc.com/news/entertainment-arts-56885646 |url-status=live}}</ref>

== Winners and nominees ==
<!-- Please do not add any fact or statement below unless you have a credible source verifying it. Otherwise, it will be promptly removed. -->

The nominees for the 93rd Academy Awards were announced on March 15, 2021, by actress [[Priyanka Chopra]] and singer [[Nick Jonas]] during a [[Streaming media|live global stream]] originating from [[London]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Siegel |first1=Tatiana |last2=Lewis |first2=Hilary |last3=Konerman |first3=Jennifer |last4=Nordyke |first4=Kimberly |title=Oscars: 'Mank' Leads Nominees With 10 |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/oscars-list-of-nominees-updating-live-4150022/ |access-date=March 19, 2021 |work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |date=March 15, 2021 |archive-date=May 5, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210505231429/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/oscars-list-of-nominees-updating-live-4150022/ |url-status=live}}</ref> ''[[Mank]]'' led all nominees with ten nominations. The winners were announced during the awards ceremony on April 25.<ref>{{cite news |title='Nomadland' Wins Best Picture, and Other Highlights from the 2021 Academy Awards |url=https://www.tampabay.com/life-culture/arts/movies/2021/04/25/oscars-updates-highlights-from-the-2021-academy-awards/ |access-date=April 30, 2021 |work=[[Tampa Bay Times]] |date=April 25, 2021 |archive-date=April 29, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210429095706/https://www.tampabay.com/life-culture/arts/movies/2021/04/25/oscars-updates-highlights-from-the-2021-academy-awards/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Chinese filmmaker [[Chloé Zhao]] became the first [[woman of color]] to win Best Director and the second woman overall after [[Kathryn Bigelow]], who won at the [[82nd Academy Awards|2010 ceremony]] for directing ''[[The Hurt Locker]]''.<ref name="NYT">{{cite news |first1=Brooks |last1=Barnes |first2=Nicole |last2=Sperling |title='Nomadland' Makes History, and Anthony Hopkins, in Upset, Wins Best Actor |date=April 25, 2021 |work=[[The New York Times]] |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/04/25/movies/academy-awards-oscars.html |access-date=April 26, 2021 |url-access=limited |archive-date=April 27, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210427205345/https://www.nytimes.com/2021/04/25/movies/academy-awards-oscars.html |url-status=live}}</ref> In addition, the nomination for [[Emerald Fennell]] in the same category meant that this also marked the first time two women directors had been nominated for the Oscar for Best Director in the same year.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Aurthur |first1=Kate |title=Oscars Make History by Nominating Two Women Directors |url=https://variety.com/2021/film/news/chloe-zhao-emerald-fennell-best-director-oscar-nominations-1234930889/ |work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=March 15, 2021 |access-date=July 1, 2025 |archive-date=April 21, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210421043804/https://variety.com/2021/film/news/chloe-zhao-emerald-fennell-best-director-oscar-nominations-1234930889/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Zhao became the first woman to receive four nominations in a single year.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Galuppo |first1=Mia |title=Oscars: Female Directors Break Record for Most Nominations in One Year |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/oscars-female-directors-break-record-for-most-nominations-in-one-year-4148628/ |work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |date=March 15, 2021 |access-date=August 18, 2026 |archive-date=June 27, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210627195847/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/oscars-female-directors-break-record-for-most-nominations-in-one-year-4148628/ |url-status=live}}</ref> For the first time all films nominated for [[Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay|Best Original Screenplay]] were also nominated for [[Academy Award for Best Picture|Best Picture]].<ref name="BBCfacts">{{cite web |last1=McIntosh |first1=Steven |title=Oscars 2021: 19 geeky facts from Borat to Boseman |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/entertainment-arts-55325109 |publisher=[[BBC]] |date=March 15, 2021 |access-date=August 17, 2026 |archive-date=April 21, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210421000528/https://www.bbc.com/news/entertainment-arts-55325109 |url-status=live}}</ref>

At age 83, [[Anthony Hopkins]] became [[List of oldest and youngest Academy Award winners and nominees#Oldest nominees 2|the oldest Best Actor nominee ever]]<ref>{{cite web |last1=Nolfi |first1=Joey |title=Anthony Hopkins is the oldest Best Actor Oscar nominee ever |url=https://ew.com/awards/oscars/anthony-hopkins-oldest-best-actor-oscars-nominee/ |work=[[Entertainment Weekly]] |date=March 15, 2021 |access-date=August 17, 2026 |archive-date=April 21, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210421191931/https://ew.com/awards/oscars/anthony-hopkins-oldest-best-actor-oscars-nominee/ |url-status=live}}</ref> and the oldest performer to win a competitive acting Oscar.<ref>{{cite news |last=Stevens |first=Matt |date=April 26, 2021 |title=Anthony Hopkins shocks by winning best actor over Chadwick Boseman. |language=en-US |work=[[The New York Times]] |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/04/25/movies/anthony-hopkins-chadwick-boseman.html |access-date=April 26, 2021 |issn=0362-4331 |url-access=limited |archive-date=April 26, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210426041854/https://www.nytimes.com/2021/04/25/movies/anthony-hopkins-chadwick-boseman.html |url-status=live}}</ref> Best Actress winner [[Frances McDormand]] became the seventh person to [[List of actors with two or more Academy Awards in acting categories|win a third acting Oscar]], the third to win three leading performance Oscars, and the second to win Best Actress three times.<ref>{{cite news |date=April 25, 2021 |title=Frances McDormand Wins Best Actress: Third Career Oscar, Only Katharine Hepburn Won More in Category |url=https://www.indiewire.com/2021/04/frances-mcdormand-wins-oscar-best-actress-nomadland-1234632159/ |last=Lindahl |first=Chris |access-date=April 26, 2021 |work=[[IndieWire]] |language=en |archive-date=April 26, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210426031412/https://www.indiewire.com/2021/04/frances-mcdormand-wins-oscar-best-actress-nomadland-1234632159/ |url-status=live}}</ref> As a producer of ''[[Nomadland]]'', she also was the first woman in history to be nominated for both acting and producing the same film,<ref name="BBCfacts"/> as well as the first person to win for both.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.billboard.com/music/awards/her-jon-batiste-record-setters-2021-oscars-9562789/ |title=H.E.R., Jon Batiste and All the Record-Setters From the 2021 Oscars |last=Grein |first=Paul |date=April 26, 2021 |work=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] |access-date=August 17, 2026 |archive-date=December 9, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211209191825/https://www.billboard.com/music/awards/her-jon-batiste-record-setters-2021-oscars-9562789/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

Best Supporting Actress winner [[Yuh-jung Youn]] became the first Korean performer and second Asian woman to win an acting Oscar after [[Miyoshi Umeki]], who won the same category for her role in 1957's ''[[Sayonara (1957 film)|Sayonara]]''.<ref name="NYT"/> With his nominations in Best Supporting Actor and Best Original Song for ''[[One Night in Miami...]]'', [[Leslie Odom Jr.]] was the fourth consecutive person to earn acting and songwriting nominations for the same film.{{efn|The three previous individuals to have earned this distinction are [[Mary J. Blige]] for ''[[Mudbound (film)|Mudbound]]'', [[Lady Gaga]] for ''[[A Star Is Born (2018 film)|A Star Is Born]]'', and [[Cynthia Erivo]] for ''[[Harriet (film)|Harriet]]''.<ref>{{cite magazine |last1=Grain |first1=Paul |title=Six Oscar Nominees Who Set New Records for Song and Score |url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/oscars/9549775/oscar-nominees-new-records-song-score |access-date=April 12, 2021 |magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] |date=April 6, 2021 |archive-date=April 2, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210402182305/https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/oscars/9549775/oscar-nominees-new-records-song-score/ |url-status=live}}</ref>}}

=== Jean Hersholt Humanitarian Awards ===
* [[Motion Picture & Television Fund]] – for the emotional and financial relief services it offers to members of the entertainment industry.<ref name="Humanitarian" />

* [[Tyler Perry]] – for his active engagement with philanthropy and charitable endeavors in recent years, including efforts to address homelessness and economic difficulties faced by members of the African-American community.<ref name="Humanitarian">{{cite news |url=https://variety.com/2021/awards/features/oscars-tyler-perry-motion-picture-television-fund-jean-hersholt-humanitarian-award-1234957330/ |title=Oscars Big Week: Tyler Perry and Motion Picture & Television Fund To Receive Jean Hersholt Humanitarian Award |last=Jackson |first=Angelique |date=April 21, 2021 |work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |access-date=April 25, 2021 |archive-date=April 26, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210426005754/https://variety.com/2021/awards/features/oscars-tyler-perry-motion-picture-television-fund-jean-hersholt-humanitarian-award-1234957330/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

== Ceremony ==
[[File:Los Angeles Union Station Ticket Lobby.jpg|thumb|The original ticket lobby of [[Union Station (Los Angeles)|Los Angeles Union Station]], where the ceremony was held]]

In April 2017, the Academy scheduled the 93rd ceremony for February 28, 2021.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Hipes |first1=Patrick |title=Oscars Dates Set For 2018 And Beyond |url=https://deadline.com/2017/04/oscars-2018-airdate-abc-academy-awards-dates-1202061171/ |access-date=June 22, 2020 |work=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |date=April 4, 2017 |archive-date=April 5, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170405053317/http://deadline.com/2017/04/oscars-2018-airdate-abc-academy-awards-dates-1202061171/ |url-status=live}}</ref> But due to the effects of the [[COVID-19 pandemic]] on both [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on cinema|cinema]] and [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on television in the United States|television]], the AMPAS Board of Governors changed the date to April 25.<ref name="Varietypostpone">{{cite news |last1=Malkin |first1=Marc |title=Oscars 2021 Pushed Back by Two Months |url=https://variety.com/2020/film/news/oscars-2021-postponed-coronavirus-1234635457/ |access-date=September 19, 2020 |work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=June 15, 2020 |archive-date=June 16, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200616010655/https://variety.com/2020/film/news/oscars-2021-postponed-coronavirus-1234635457/ |url-status=live}}</ref> The annual Academy Governors Awards and corresponding nominees luncheon were canceled due to COVID-19 safety concerns.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Pond |first1=Steve |title=Academy Limits Oscars to Nominees and Their Guests, Cancels Governors Ball and Nominees Lunch |url=https://www.thewrap.com/academy-limits-oscars-to-nominees-and-their-guests-cancels-governors-ball-and-nominees-lunch/ |access-date=May 30, 2021 |work=[[TheWrap]] |date=March 15, 2021 |archive-date=June 3, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210603065351/https://www.thewrap.com/academy-limits-oscars-to-nominees-and-their-guests-cancels-governors-ball-and-nominees-lunch/ |url-status=live}}</ref> This marked the first time since the [[60th Academy Awards|60th ceremony]] held in 1988 that the awards were held in April.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Finn |first1=Natalie |title=The 7 Biggest Jaw-Droppers at the 2021 Oscars |url=https://www.eonline.com/news/1262414/the-7-biggest-jaw-droppers-at-the-2021-oscars |access-date=June 17, 2021 |agency=[[E!]] |date=April 26, 2021 |archive-date=June 24, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210624201824/https://www.eonline.com/news/1262414/the-7-biggest-jaw-droppers-at-the-2021-oscars |url-status=live}}</ref> It was the fourth time in history that the ceremony was postponed from its original date (following the [[10th Academy Awards|10th ceremony]] in 1938, the [[40th Academy Awards|40th ceremony]] in 1968, and the [[53rd Academy Awards|53rd ceremony]] in 1981).<ref name="Varietypostpone"/>

In December 2020, the Academy hired television producer Jesse Collins, film producer [[Stacey Sher]], and Oscar-winning director [[Steven Soderbergh]] to oversee production of the telecast. "The upcoming Oscars is the perfect occasion for innovation and for re-envisioning the possibilities for the awards show. This is a dream team who will respond directly to these times. The Academy is excited to work with them to deliver an event that reflects the worldwide love of movies and how they connect us and entertain us when we need them the most", said Academy president David Rubin and CEO [[Dawn Hudson]].<ref name="Producers">{{cite news |last1=Hammond |first1=Pete |title=Oscars: Steven Soderbergh, Stacey Sher & Jesse Collins To Produce 93rd Academy Awards |url=https://deadline.com/2020/12/oscars-steven-soderbergh-stacey-sher-jesse-collins-producers-academ-awardsto-produce-93rd-academy-awards-1234652331/ |access-date=December 30, 2020 |work=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |date=December 8, 2020 |archive-date=December 28, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201228033747/https://deadline.com/2020/12/oscars-steven-soderbergh-stacey-sher-jesse-collins-producers-academ-awardsto-produce-93rd-academy-awards-1234652331/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

The tagline for the ceremony, "Bring Your Movie Love", was intended to reflect "our global appreciation for the power of film to foster connection, to educate, and to inspire us to tell our own stories". In tandem with the theme, the Academy hired seven artists to create custom posters for the event inspired by the question "What do movies mean to you?"<ref name="Posters">{{cite news |last1=Hipes |first1=Patrick |title=Oscars Poster Revealed With This Year's Tagline "Bring Your Movie Love"; No Clues Offered About Ceremony |url=https://deadline.com/2021/03/oscars-2021-poster-key-art-revealed-1234712398/ |access-date=June 19, 2021 |work=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |date=March 11, 2021 |archive-date=June 24, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210624200758/https://deadline.com/2021/03/oscars-2021-poster-key-art-revealed-1234712398/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Another aspect of the telecast's production was to produce the ceremony as if it were a film, including promoting the presenters as a "cast",<ref>{{cite news |last=Hammond |first=Pete |date=April 12, 2021 |title=Oscars: Academy Sets Ensemble Cast Of 15 Stars To Serve As Presenters |url=https://deadline.com/2021/04/academy-announces-ensemble-cast-of-15-stars-to-serve-as-presenters-on-oscar-show-1234732531/ |url-status=live |access-date=April 12, 2021 |work=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |language=en-US |archive-date=April 17, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210417231425/https://deadline.com/2021/04/academy-announces-ensemble-cast-of-15-stars-to-serve-as-presenters-on-oscar-show-1234732531/}}</ref><ref name=":4">{{cite news |last1=Hammond |first1=Pete |title=Oscar Show Takes Shape With Letter To Nominees: No Zooms, No Casual Dress, Covid Protocols In Force & "Stories Matter" |url=https://deadline.com/2021/03/oscar-show-takes-shape-no-zooms-producers-strtess-covid-safety-1234717664/ |access-date=March 22, 2021 |work=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |date=March 18, 2021 |archive-date=March 23, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210323002728/https://deadline.com/2021/03/oscar-show-takes-shape-no-zooms-producers-strtess-covid-safety-1234717664/ |url-status=live}}</ref> being filmed at the traditional cinematic [[frame rate]] of [[24p|24 frames per-second]] as opposed to 30, and using a cinematic [[aspect ratio]] rather than the standard [[16:9 aspect ratio]] used by most television programming.<ref>{{cite news |last=Van Syckle |first=Katie |date=April 22, 2021 |title=Preparing for a Surreal Oscar Night |work=[[The New York Times]] |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/04/22/insider/Oscars-Covid-pandemic.html |access-date=April 26, 2021 |url-access=limited |archive-date=April 25, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210425165122/https://www.nytimes.com/2021/04/22/insider/Oscars-Covid-pandemic.html |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Framke |first=Caroline |date=April 25, 2021 |title=Oscar Telecast's Best Creative Decisions Got Lost in Forced Format Changes: TV Review |work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |url=https://variety.com/2021/tv/news/oscars-review-academy-awards-2021-1234960324/ |access-date=August 18, 2026 |archive-date=April 26, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210426035740/https://variety.com/2021/tv/news/oscars-review-academy-awards-2021-1234960324/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

Because of the pandemic, AMPAS announced that the main ceremony would be held for the first time at [[Union Station (Los Angeles)|Union Station]] in [[Downtown Los Angeles]], with parts of the festivities at the [[Dolby Theatre]] in Hollywood, the ceremony's usual venue.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Maddus |first1=Gene |title=Oscars to Broadcast From L.A.'s Union Station and Dolby Theatre |url=https://variety.com/2021/film/awards/oscars-to-broadcast-from-l-a-s-union-station-and-dolby-theatre-1234929614/ |access-date=March 25, 2021 |work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=March 15, 2021 |archive-date=March 24, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210324133246/https://variety.com/2021/film/awards/oscars-to-broadcast-from-l-a-s-union-station-and-dolby-theatre-1234929614/ |url-status=live}}</ref> To satisfy health and safety protocols, the Academy limited the number of people attending the gala to primarily nominees and presenters.<ref name=":4"/><ref>{{cite news |last1=Feinberg |first1=Scott |title=Oscars: Only Presenters, Nominees and Guests Will Attend In-Person |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/general-news/oscars-only-presenters-nominees-and-guests-will-attend-in-person-4150656/ |access-date=April 12, 2021 |work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |date=March 15, 2021 |archive-date=June 24, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210624201709/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/general-news/oscars-only-presenters-nominees-and-guests-will-attend-in-person-4150656/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Attendees were asked to submit travel plans to Oscar organizers before arriving in Los Angeles, take multiple [[COVID-19 testing in the United States|COVID-19 tests]], and isolate for ten days before the event.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Rottenberg |first1=Josh |title=Masks at the Oscars? Here's How the Academy Awards are Happening in Person |url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/movies/story/2021-04-25/oscars-2021-in-person-masks-red-carpet-covid-rules |access-date=May 16, 2021 |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=April 25, 2021 |url-access=limited |archive-date=May 16, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210516055003/https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/movies/story/2021-04-25/oscars-2021-in-person-masks-red-carpet-covid-rules |url-status=live}}</ref> Guests were also asked to wear masks when the broadcast paused for commercial breaks.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Malkin |first1=Marc |title=Oscar Attendees Will Not Wear Face Masks During Telecast (Exclusive) |url=https://variety.com/2021/tv/awards/oscars-attendees-masks-covid-1234954802/ |access-date=May 20, 2021 |work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=April 19, 2021 |archive-date=April 22, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210422214542/https://variety.com/2021/tv/awards/oscars-attendees-masks-covid-1234954802/ |url-status=live}}</ref> In consideration of overseas nominees unable to attend the ceremony, producers set up satellite "hubs", such as at [[BFI Southbank]] in London, where they could participate in the gala.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Hammond |first1=Pete |title=Oscars: Academy To Create European Hub(s) For Nominees Unable To Travel To U.S.; Producers Reveal New Details On Show |url=https://deadline.com/2021/03/oscars-update-academy-to-create-european-hubs-for-nominees-unable-to-travel-to-u-s-1234724601/ |access-date=April 12, 2021 |work=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |date=March 30, 2021 |archive-date=April 10, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210410233312/https://deadline.com/2021/03/oscars-update-academy-to-create-european-hubs-for-nominees-unable-to-travel-to-u-s-1234724601/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Ravindran |first1=Manori |title=Oscars in London: BFI Southbank Confirmed as U.K. Hub For Ceremony (Exclusive) |url=https://variety.com/2021/film/global/oscars-2021-london-event-bfi-southbank-1234950221/ |access-date=May 7, 2021 |work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=April 14, 2021 |archive-date=April 23, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210423233808/https://variety.com/2021/film/global/oscars-2021-london-event-bfi-southbank-1234950221/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Additionally, the five Best Original Song nominees were performed in previously recorded segments shown during the red carpet pre-show. Four of the songs were performed atop the Dolby Family Terrace of the [[Academy Museum of Motion Pictures]]; "[[Husavik (song)|Husavik]]" from ''[[Eurovision Song Contest: The Story of Fire Saga]]'' was performed on location in the song's [[Húsavík|namesake town in Iceland]].<ref name="Husavik"/>

[[The Roots]] musician and ''[[The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon|The Tonight Show]]'' bandleader [[Questlove]] served as musical director for the ceremony.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://variety.com/2021/music/news/questlove-music-2021-oscars-1234956085/ |date=April 21, 2021 |work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |title=How Questlove and Oscars Producer Jesse Collins Are |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210425225840/https://variety.com/2021/music/news/questlove-music-2021-oscars-1234956085/ |url-status=live}}</ref> He, Oscars red carpet pre-show host [[Ariana DeBose]], and actor [[Lin-Manuel Miranda]] presented trailers for the upcoming films ''[[Summer of Soul (...Or, When the Revolution Could Not Be Televised)]]'', ''[[West Side Story (2021 film)|West Side Story]]'', and ''[[In the Heights (film)|In the Heights]]'', respectively, during the ceremony.<ref name="trailer">{{cite news |date=April 22, 2021 |first=Brian |last=Welk |title='West |access-date=April 22, 2021 |work=[[TheWrap]] |url-status=live |archive-date=April 23, 2021 2021 |first=Anthony |last=D'Alessandro |title=Disney To Celebrate Moviegoing During Oscars With Talent & Exclusive Trailers From 'West Side Story', 'Summer Of Soul' & More |url=https://deadline.com/2021/04/disney-oscars-moviegoing-celebration-west-side-story-summer-of-soul-trailers-1234742010/ |access-date=April 22, 2021 |work=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |url-status=live 28, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210428024850/https://variety.com/2021/artisans/awards/oscars-production-design-union-station-1234957462/ |url-status=live}}</ref> In a press |url=https://deadline.com/2021/04/oscars-union-station-venue-production-photo-gallery-1234741303/ |url-status=live |access-date=April 23, 2021 |work=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |language=en-US |archive-date=April 22, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210422185013/https://deadline.com/2021/04/oscars-union-station-venue-production-photo-gallery-1234741303/}}</ref> He also cited |url=https://www.thewrap.com/oscars-song-contenders-perform-pre-show-after-dark-special/ |work=[[TheWrap]] |date=April 16, 2021 |access-date=April 26, 2021 |archive-date=April 26, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210426040158/https://www.thewrap.com/oscars-song-contenders-perform-pre-show-after-dark-special/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

The ceremony offered accommodations for those who are deaf or visually impaired; it was the first Academy Awards to be broadcast with [[audio description]] for the visually impaired (carried via [[second audio program]] on the ABC telecast), which (along with its closed captioning) was sponsored by [[Google]]. A [[sign language interpreter]] was available in the media room. Deaf actress [[Marlee Matlin]] served as one of the award presenters, with her longtime partner Jack Jason interpreting her [[American Sign Language]] to spoken English.<ref>{{Cite web |last=White |first=Abbey |date=2022-03-25 |title=Oscars Telecast Will Feature Free Live ASL Interpretation on The Academy's YouTube Channel |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/oscars-2022-show-asl-interpretation-live-stream-accessibility-disability-1235118372/ |access-date=2022-03-29 |website=The Hollywood Reporter |language=en-US |archive-date=March 27, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220327194529/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/oscars-2022-show-asl-interpretation-live-stream-accessibility-disability-1235118372/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Sun |first=Rebecca |date=2021-04-26 |title=Oscars Diversity: Historic Firsts for Non-Acting Categories and Ceremony Accessibility |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/oscars-diversity-historic-firsts-for-non-acting-categories-and-ceremony-accessibility-4173310/ |access-date=2022-03-29 |website=The Hollywood Reporter |language=en-US |archive-date=March 29, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220329003956/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/oscars-diversity-historic-firsts-for-non-acting-categories-and-ceremony-accessibility-4173310/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-01-04 |title=Marlee Matlin on 'CODA' & Fighting for Deaf Stories |url=https://www.backstage.com/magazine/article/marlee-matlin-coda-73648/ |access-date=2022-03-28 |website=Backstage |archive-date=December 4, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211204121834/https://www.backstage.com/magazine/article/marlee-matlin-coda-73648/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

===Eligibility and other rule changes===
Due to the date change, the Academy changed the eligibility deadline for feature films from December 31, 2020, to February 28, 2021. AMPAS president Rubin and CEO Hudson explained the decision to extend the eligibility period, saying: "For over a century, movies have played an important role in comforting, inspiring, and entertaining us during the darkest of times. They certainly have this year. Our hope, in extending the eligibility period and our Awards date, is to provide the flexibility filmmakers need to finish and release their films without being penalized for something beyond anyone's control."<ref>{{cite news |last1=Barnes |first1=Brooks |title=The 2021 Oscars Will Be Delayed |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2020/06/15/business/media/2021-oscars-delayed-coronavirus.html |access-date=August 13, 2020 |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=June 15, 2020 |url-access=limited |archive-date=August 21, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200821192505/https://www.nytimes.com/2020/06/15/business/media/2021-oscars-delayed-coronavirus.html |url-status=live}}</ref>

The Academy also revised its release and distribution requirements by making films released via [[video on demand]] or [[streaming]] eligible for the awards as long as they were originally scheduled to have a theatrical release and were uploaded to AMPAS's online screening service within 60 days of their public release. AMPAS also amended its theatrical exhibition qualifying rules to allow films debuting in theaters in New York City, Chicago, the San Francisco Bay Area, Atlanta, and Miami to qualify for the awards in addition to venues in Los Angeles.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Feinberg |first1=Scott |title=Oscars During Coronavirus: Academy Rules Streamed Films Eligible, Merges Sound Categories |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/general-news/oscars-coronavirus-academy-rules-streamed-films-eligible-merges-sound-categories-1292043/ |access-date=June 19, 2020 |work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |date=April 28, 2020 |archive-date=June 24, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210624201256/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/general-news/oscars-coronavirus-academy-rules-streamed-films-eligible-merges-sound-categories-1292043/ |url-status=live}}</ref> A week of nightly screenings at a [[drive-in theater]] in the aforementioned cities also made films eligible for consideration.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Mandell |first1=Andrea |last2=Alexander |first2=Bryan |title=Academy Makes Major Change: Drive-in Movies Can Now Qualify for 2021 Oscars |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/entertainment/movies/2020/10/07/oscars-academy-says-drive-movies-qualify-2021-ceremony/5917312002/ |access-date=November 17, 2020 |work=[[USA Today]] |date=October 7, 2020 |archive-date=November 6, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201106132251/https://www.usatoday.com/story/entertainment/movies/2020/10/07/oscars-academy-says-drive-movies-qualify-2021-ceremony/5917312002/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

Furthermore, the Academy made changes to specific award categories. The [[Best Sound Mixing]] and [[Academy Award for Best Sound Editing|Best Sound Editing]] categories were combined into a single Best Sound category (which had existed from the [[3rd Academy Awards|3rd Awards]] in 1930 through the [[75th Academy Awards|75th Awards]] in 2003) due to concerns from the Sound branch that the two categories had developed too much overlap in scope.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Ordoña |first1=Michael |title=Just One Oscar Category for Sound? The Pros Are Happy to Share the Acclaim |url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/movies/story/2020-04-28/just-one-sound-category-the-pros-are-delighted-since-the-two-jobs-lines-have-blurred |access-date=August 12, 2020 |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=April 28, 2020 |url-access=limited |archive-date=June 21, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200621012009/https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/movies/story/2020-04-28/just-one-sound-category-the-pros-are-delighted-since-the-two-jobs-lines-have-blurred |url-status=live}}</ref> The rules for [[Academy Award for Best Original Score|Best Original Score]] were changed to require that a film's score include a minimum of 60% original music, with franchise films and sequels required to have a minimum of 80% new music.<ref>{{cite magazine |last1=Grein |first1=Paul |title=Oscars Extend Eligibility to Streamed Films Amid Coronavirus Pandemic |url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/awards/9367595/oscars-rules-change-streamed-films-coronavirus |access-date=June 29, 2020 |magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] |date=April 28, 2020 |archive-date=June 4, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200604111537/https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/awards/9367595/oscars-rules-change-streamed-films-coronavirus |url-status=live}}</ref> Finally, preliminary voting for [[Best International Feature Film]] was opened to all voting members of the Academy for the first time.<ref>{{cite news |last=Hammond |first=Pete |date=April 28, 2020 |title=Oscars Keeping Show Date But Make Big News As Academy Lightens Eligibility Rules, Combines Sound Categories, Ends DVD Screeners and More |url=https://deadline.com/2020/04/oscars-major-changes-academy-awards-coronavirus-1202919950/ |access-date=May 6, 2020 |work=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |language=en |archive-date=May 23, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200523043653/https://deadline.com/2020/04/oscars-major-changes-academy-awards-coronavirus-1202919950/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Best Actor announcement ending ===
[[File:Chadwick Boseman by Gage Skidmore July 2017 (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|alt=Chadwick Boseman in 2017.|Many viewers and television critics believed [[Chadwick Boseman]]'s impending win for Best Actor was a reason that producers saved the category as the last to be presented at the ceremony.]]

In a break with tradition, the lead acting categories were presented last after the awarding of Best Picture, with Best Actor coming last.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Vary |first1=Adam B. |title=Oscars End Abruptly with Anthony Hopkins Best Actor Upset |url=https://variety.com/2021/awards/news/anthony-hopkins-best-actor-oscar-upset-1234959766/ |access-date=April 30, 2021 |work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=April 25, 2021 |archive-date=April 26, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210426162709/https://variety.com/2021/awards/news/anthony-hopkins-best-actor-oscar-upset-1234959766/ |url-status=live}}</ref> This led many viewers to believe that the ceremony's producers were anticipating Chadwick Boseman posthumously winning Best Actor, which could have been accompanied by a tribute to the actor; Boseman had been considered a strong frontrunner for the award.<ref name="Hopkins Reacts">{{cite news |last1=Jackson |first1=Angelique |title=Anthony Hopkins Pays Tribute to Chadwick Boseman After Surprise Second Oscar Win |url=https://variety.com/2021/awards/news/anthony-hopkins-oscar-win-reaction-1234960502/ |access-date=July 2, 2021 |work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=April 26, 2021 |archive-date=July 10, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210710075831/https://variety.com/2021/awards/news/anthony-hopkins-oscar-win-reaction-1234960502/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Abrupt ending">{{cite news |last1=Buchanan |first1=Kyle |title=Inside Anthony Hopkins's Unexpected Win at the Oscars |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/04/26/movies/the-father-anthony-hopkins-oscars.html |access-date=May 23, 2021 |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=April 26, 2021 |url-access=limited |archive-date=May 15, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210515101153/https://www.nytimes.com/2021/04/26/movies/the-father-anthony-hopkins-oscars.html |url-status=live}}</ref> When presenter [[Joaquin Phoenix]] announced that Anthony Hopkins was the winner, Phoenix said that the Academy accepted the award on behalf of Hopkins, who was not present, and the ceremony came to an abrupt end.<ref name="Abrupt ending" /> It was later reported that Hopkins, who did not want to travel from his home in Wales, offered to appear via [[Zoom (software)|Zoom]], but the producers declined his request.<ref name="Abrupt ending"/>

The day after the ceremony, Hopkins released an acceptance speech on Instagram, in which he thanked the Academy, said that he "really did not expect" to win, and paid tribute to Boseman.<ref name="Hopkins Reacts" /> The selection of Hopkins over Boseman was controversial,<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Drury |first1=Sharareh |date=2021-04-26 |title=Oscars Face Backlash Over Chadwick Boseman Snub |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/oscars-criticized-chadwick-boseman-snub-4173199/ |access-date=2022-04-02 |website=The Hollywood Reporter |language=en-US |archive-date=April 2, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220402085207/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/oscars-criticized-chadwick-boseman-snub-4173199/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Romero |first=Ariana |title=Chadwick Boseman Loses Best Actor In Shocking Oscars Finale |url=https://www.refinery29.com/en-us/2021/04/10443095/chadwick-boseman-oscar-best-actor-loss-twitter-reactions |access-date=2022-04-02 |website=www.refinery29.com |language=en |archive-date=April 2, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220402085055/https://www.refinery29.com/en-us/2021/04/10443095/chadwick-boseman-oscar-best-actor-loss-twitter-reactions |url-status=live}}</ref> but Boseman's brother reported the family had no hard feelings toward the Academy.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Sharf |first1=Zack |date=2021-04-27 |title=Chadwick Boseman's Family Speaks Out on Oscars Loss: This Was Not a Snub |url=https://www.indiewire.com/2021/04/chadwick-boseman-family-oscars-snub-1234633534/ |access-date=2022-04-02 |website=IndieWire |language=en |archive-date=April 2, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220402085055/https://www.indiewire.com/2021/04/chadwick-boseman-family-oscars-snub-1234633534/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

In an interview, Soderbergh said that switching the traditional order of awards was planned before the nominations were announced, saying, "actors' speeches tend to be more dramatic than producers' speeches". He said that Boseman's widow accepting the award "would have been such a shattering moment" and "there would be nowhere to go after that". Soderbergh also defended the decision to not allow acceptance speeches via Zoom.<ref>{{cite news |date=May 4, 2021 |title=That off-key Oscars ending? Had to be done, says producer Steven Soderbergh |url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/movies/story/2021-05-04/steven-soderbergh-oscars-ending-chadwick-boseman-anthony-hopkins |access-date=May 13, 2021 |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |language=en-US |url-access=limited |archive-date=May 13, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210513012655/https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/movies/story/2021-05-04/steven-soderbergh-oscars-ending-chadwick-boseman-anthony-hopkins |url-status=live}}</ref>

===Critical reviews===
Many media outlets received the broadcast negatively.<ref name="Makeover"/><ref name="BBC Review"/> {{Rotten Tomatoes prose|24|3=34|4=The 93rd Oscars definitely delivered something different, but after a strong opening moment with Regina King, the changes to this year's ceremony cemented the importance of certain structural traditions -- and how damaging hedging your bets on the Academy's votes can be.|ref=y|access-date=March 15, 2024}}<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Academy Awards: 93rd Oscars |url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/tv/the_academy_awards/s93 |access-date=2024-03-15 |website=[[Rotten Tomatoes]] |publisher=[[Fandango Media]] |language=en |archive-date=April 26, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210426061053/https://www.rottentomatoes.com/tv/the_academy_awards/s93 |url-status=live }}</ref> Television critic Mike Hale of ''[[The New York Times]]'' wrote, "Sunday's broadcast on ABC was more like a cross between the [[Golden Globes]] and the closing-night banquet of a long, exhausting convention." He also commented, "The trade-off — whether because of the smaller crowd, the social distancing, or the sound quality in the cavernous space — was what felt like a dead room, both acoustically and emotionally. There were powerful and moving speeches, but they didn't seem to be generating much excitement, and when the people in the room aren't excited, it's hard to get excited at home."<ref>{{cite news |last1=Hale |first1=Mike |title=The Covid-19 Oscars: Not Masked but Still Muffled |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/04/25/arts/television/covid-19-oscars-2021.html |access-date=May 9, 2021 |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=April 25, 2021 |url-access=limited |archive-date=May 9, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210509134351/https://www.nytimes.com/2021/04/25/arts/television/covid-19-oscars-2021.html |url-status=live}}</ref> ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' columnist [[Rob Sheffield]] noted, "The most flamboyantly unplanned and half-assed Oscar Night in recent history was a grind from beginning to end." He also criticized the production of the "In Memoriam" segment saying that the montage was edited at an inappropriately fast pace.<ref>{{cite magazine |last1=Sheffield |first1=Rob |author-link=Rob Sheffield |title=Oscars 2021: Wolf Howls, Da Butt and the Chadwick Boseman Tribute That Wasn't |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/movies/movie-features/oscars-2021-da-butt-rob-sheffield-1161148/ |access-date=May 17, 2021 |magazine=[[Rolling Stone]] |date=April 25, 2021 |url-access=limited |archive-date=May 4, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210504200824/https://www.rollingstone.com/movies/movie-features/oscars-2021-da-butt-rob-sheffield-1161148/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Kelly Lawler of ''[[USA Today]]'' commented, "While it was certainly challenging to stage the show safely, [[63rd Annual Grammy Awards|last month's Grammys]] proved that it is possible to make something entertaining and engaging amid the pandemic. Unfortunately, the Oscars producers seemingly missed that show. The Oscars were a train wreck at the train station, an excruciatingly long, boring telecast that lacked the verve of so many movies we love."<ref>{{cite news |last1=Lawler |first1=Kelly |title=How the First (and Hopefully Last) Pandemic Oscars Went So Terribly Wrong |url=https://www.usatoday.com/in-depth/entertainment/tv/2021/04/26/oscars-2021-review-how-pandemic-ceremony-went-so-terribly-wrong/7292897002/ |access-date=May 23, 2021 |work=[[USA Today]] |date=April 26, 2021 |url-access=limited |archive-date=May 31, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210531090925/https://www.usatoday.com/in-depth/entertainment/tv/2021/04/26/oscars-2021-review-how-pandemic-ceremony-went-so-terribly-wrong/7292897002/ |url-status=dead}}</ref>

Others gave a more favorable review of the show. ''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]'' columnist Judy Berman wrote that the ceremony "was more entertaining than the average pre-COVID Oscars. It started out especially strong." She added, "Every part of this year's ceremony felt more intimate and less stuffy than just about any awards show I can remember. For once, the art and community of film seemed to take precedence over the business of film."<ref>{{cite magazine |last1=Berman |first1=Judy |title=The Pandemic Oscars Were Surprisingly Decent. But Will the Academy Learn Anything From Its Break With Tradition? |url=https://time.com/5958414/oscars-review-2021/ |access-date=May 31, 2021 |magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]] |date=April 26, 2021 |archive-date=April 29, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210429165333/https://time.com/5958414/oscars-review-2021/ |url-status=live}}</ref> [[Associated Press]] reporter Lindsey Bahr commented, "The 93rd Academy Awards wasn't exactly a movie, but it was a show made for people who love learning about movies. And it stubbornly, defiantly wasn't trying to be anything else."<ref>{{cite news |last1=Bahr |first1=Lindsey |title=Review: Not Quite a Movie, but the Oscars Were a Love Letter |url=https://apnews.com/article/oscars-2021-review-c02d5d74c3615c74b81aa82af3df570f |access-date=May 31, 2021 |work=[[Associated Press]] |date=April 25, 2021 |archive-date=June 2, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210602214146/https://apnews.com/article/oscars-2021-review-c02d5d74c3615c74b81aa82af3df570f |url-status=live}}</ref> Darren Franich of ''[[Entertainment Weekly]]'' gave an average review of the telecast, but singled out the winners and presenters for providing memorable moments throughout the show.<ref>{{cite magazine |last1=Franich |first1=Darren |title=What a Weird Oscars: Review |url=https://ew.com/awards/oscars/oscars-2021-review/ |access-date=May 25, 2021 |magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]] |date=April 25, 2021 |archive-date=May 21, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210521092711/https://ew.com/awards/oscars/oscars-2021-review/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

===Ratings and reception===
The American telecast on ABC drew in an average of 10.4 million people over its length, which was a 56% decrease from the [[92nd Academy Awards|previous year's ceremony]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Richwine |first1=Lisa |last2=Grebler |first2=Dan |title=Final TV ratings for Oscars inch up to 10.4 million viewers |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-awards-oscars-ratings-idCAKBN2CE2D6 |access-date=June 19, 2021 |work=[[Reuters]] |date=April 27, 2021 |archive-date=June 24, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210624202839/https://www.reuters.com/article/us-awards-oscars-ratings-idCAKBN2CE2D6 |url-status=live}}</ref> The show also earned lower [[Nielsen ratings]] compared to the previous ceremony with 5.9% of households watching the ceremony.<ref name="TVB" /> In addition, it garnered a lower rating among viewers between ages 18–49 with a 2.1 rating among viewers in that demographic.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Whitten |first1=Sarah |title=Audiences for Award Shows are in Steep Decline; This Chart Shows How Far Viewership Has Fallen |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2021/05/02/oscars-2021-nielsen-data-shows-viewers-have-lost-interest-in-award-shows.html |access-date=May 19, 2021 |agency=[[CNBC]] |date=May 2, 2021 |archive-date=May 19, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210519013517/https://www.cnbc.com/2021/05/02/oscars-2021-nielsen-data-shows-viewers-have-lost-interest-in-award-shows.html |url-status=live}}</ref> It earned the lowest viewership for an Academy Award telecast since figures were compiled beginning with the [[46th Academy Awards|46th ceremony]] in 1974.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Smith |first1=Gerry |title=Oscars Audience Collapses in Latest Setback for Awards Shows |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-04-26/oscars-audience-falls-by-over-half-in-latest-setback-for-awards |access-date=June 19, 2021 |work=[[Bloomberg Businessweek]] |date=April 26, 2021 |archive-date=April 29, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210429232051/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-04-26/oscars-audience-falls-by-over-half-in-latest-setback-for-awards |url-status=live}}</ref> Moreover, the show did not make the list of the 100 most watched telecasts in the United States in 2021, while previous ceremonies usually ranked in the top ten.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Schneider |first1=Michael |last2=Zorrilla |first2=Mónica Marie |title=Top 100 Telecasts of 2021: 'NCIS,' 'Yellowstone,' NFL Dominate, as Oscars Fail to Make the Cut |url=https://variety.com/2021/tv/news/top-rated-shows-2021-ncis-yellowstone-squid-game-1235143671/ |access-date=August 17, 2026 |work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=December 29, 2021 |archive-date=December 29, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211229183322/https://variety.com/2021/tv/news/top-rated-shows-2021-ncis-yellowstone-squid-game-1235143671/ |url-status=live}}</ref> However, it was the most watched [[awards show]] of the season.<ref name="DeadlineViews"/>

In July 2021, the ceremony presentation received four nominations for the [[73rd Primetime Emmy Awards]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Goldberg |first1=Leslie |title=Emmys: Disney Leads All Combined Nominations as HBO (Thanks to HBO Max) Tops Netflix |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/emmy-nominations-by-series-network-2021-1234981275/ |access-date=September 19, 2021 |work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |date=July 13, 2021 |archive-date=October 11, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211011030431/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/emmy-nominations-by-series-network-2021-1234981275/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Two months later, the ceremony won for [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Production Design for a Variety Special|Outstanding Production Design for a Variety Special]] (Alana Billingsley, Joe Celli, Jason Howard, and [[David Rockwell]]).<ref>{{cite news |last1=Pedersen |first1=Erik |title=Creative Arts Emmys: Complete Winners List For All Three Ceremonies |url=https://deadline.com/2021/09/creative-arts-emmy-awards-2021-winners-list-1234831219/ |access-date=November 11, 2021 |work=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |date=September 12, 2021 |archive-date=September 12, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210912000458/https://deadline.com/2021/09/creative-arts-emmy-awards-2021-winners-list-1234831219/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Censorship in China and Hong Kong===
The ceremony was subject to various forms of censorship in China and its territories. Due to scrutiny over ''Nomadland'' director [[Chloé Zhao]]—a Chinese-American citizen who reportedly made comments critical of China in a 2013 interview with ''[[Filmmaker (magazine)|Filmmaker]]'' magazine—the ceremony telecast was pulled by its local rightsholders in the mainland, and all discussions of the ceremony were [[Censorship in China|censored from Chinese social media and news outlets]].<ref>{{cite news |date=2021-04-26 |title=Chloé Zhao's historic win at this year's Oscars censored in China |url=https://www.scmp.com/lifestyle/entertainment/article/3131131/nomadland-director-chloe-zhaos-historic-oscars-win-censored |access-date=2021-04-27 |work=[[South China Morning Post]] |language=en |archive-date=October 7, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211007070954/https://www.scmp.com/lifestyle/entertainment/article/3131131/nomadland-director-chloe-zhaos-historic-oscars-win-censored |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Lin |first=Liza |date=2021-04-26 |title=China Censors 'Nomadland' Director Chloé Zhao's Oscar Win |language=en-US |work=[[The Wall Street Journal]] |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/china-censors-nomadland-director-chloe-zhaos-oscar-win-11619440550 |access-date=2021-04-26 |issn=0099-9660 |archive-date=April 29, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210429222410/https://www.wsj.com/articles/china-censors-nomadland-director-chloe-zhaos-oscar-win-11619440550 |url-status=live}}</ref>

In addition, Hong Kong broadcaster [[TVB]] announced that the ceremony would not be shown live in the region for the first time since 1969. A TVB spokesperson told [[Agence France-Presse|AFP]] that this was a "commercial decision". It was speculated that the decision was in retaliation for the nomination of ''[[Do Not Split]]'', a documentary on [[2019–2020 Hong Kong protests|Hong Kong's pro-democracy protests in 2019]], for Best Documentary Short Subject.<ref>{{cite news |date=April 25, 2021 |title=Oscars won't show in Hong Kong for first time since 1969 as state media rails against protest film nomination |url=https://hongkongfp.com/2021/03/29/oscars-wont-show-in-hong-kong-for-first-time-since-1969-as-state-media-rails-against-protest-film-nomination/ |work=[[Hong Kong Free Press]] |access-date=April 26, 2021 |archive-date=March 22, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230322081755/https://hongkongfp.com/2021/03/29/oscars-wont-show-in-hong-kong-for-first-time-since-1969-as-state-media-rails-against-protest-film-nomination/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

== "In Memoriam" ==
The annual "In Memoriam" segment was presented by [[Angela Bassett]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=D'Zurilla |first1=Christine |title=Another Oscars, Another Round of In Memoriam Snubs: Where Was Adam Schlesinger? |url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/movies/story/2021-04-26/oscars-2021-in-memoriam-snubs-adam-schlesinger |access-date=June 12, 2021 |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=April 26, 2021 |url-access=limited |archive-date=June 11, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210611150620/https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/movies/story/2021-04-26/oscars-2021-in-memoriam-snubs-adam-schlesinger |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Gittins |first=William |date=April 24, 2021 |title=In Memoriam Oscars 2021: directors, actors and writers who died in 2020 |url=https://en.as.com/en/2021/04/25/latest_news/1619317219_989708.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210425142051/https://en.as.com/en/2021/04/25/latest_news/1619317219_989708.html |archive-date=April 25, 2021 |access-date=April 27, 2021 |work=[[Diario AS]]}}</ref> The montage featured the song "[[As (song)|As]]" by singer [[Stevie Wonder]].<ref>{{cite magazine |last1=Klnane |first1=Ruth |title=Chadwick Boseman, Christopher Plummer, Sean Connery Featured in Oscars in Memoriam Tribute |url=https://ew.com/awards/oscars/oscars-in-memoriam-2021/ |access-date=June 12, 2021 |magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]] |date=April 25, 2021 |archive-date=June 13, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210613082919/https://ew.com/awards/oscars/oscars-in-memoriam-2021/ |url-status=live}}</ref>
